- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery
- **Governing policy:** *Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026)*, effective 08/04/2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon requested for me. The notice dated July 31, 2026 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and to approve the surgery, because the records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria in CMM-606.

My surgeon, Okafor, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed. Below I have set the plan's language side by side with what my records say.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The plan's framework for initial surgery.** CMM-606 states:

> "Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy or Hemilaminectomy) CMM.SP.IN.606.2 v1.0.2026 Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

This is the section that applies to me. This is an initial, not a repeat, procedure at this level.

**2. Symptoms with standing, and a failure to improve.** The policy lists, among the criteria:

> "▪ symptoms worsen with standing and/or walking ▪ symptoms are alleviated with sitting and/or forward flexion • Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

My records establish the standing limitation and the lack of meaningful improvement:

- I have had 14 months of progressive low back pain that is not relieved by rest.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.
- I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy — core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — from April 10, 2026 to July 3, 2026, 16 visits, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- I had a corticosteroid injection on April 20, 2026 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

**3. Objective examination findings.** The policy lists these findings:

> "◦ positive straight leg raise ◦ positive crossed straight leg raise ◦ positive femoral stretch test ◦ dermatomal sensory deficit ◦ functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness) ◦ reflex changes ◦ unremitting radicular pain into the lower extremity(ies) without concordant objective exam findings • Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

My records document:

- Positive provocative testing on the affected side. [Please see the specific provocative test(s) and results as recorded in the office note of [date] — [insert exact findings from the chart].]
- A neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. [Please see the exact deficit as recorded in the office note of [date].]
- Radicular pain into the right calf.
- MRI of the lumbar spine dated June 8, 2026: L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.

The imaging and the examination point to the same level and the same side. My symptoms are not unexplained pain; they correspond to a nerve root that the MRI shows is compressed.

**4. The surgeon requirement.** The policy states:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Credentialed Spine Surgeon Required • Endoscopic lumbar discectomy requires the procedure be performed by a spine surgeon with surgical privileges at a hospital, hospital outpatient department, or ambulatory surgery center to perform open surgical approach(es) for lumbar discectomy."

My surgeon is Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. [Surgeon's surgical privileges and the facility where the procedure would be performed — to be confirmed by my surgeon's office.]

**5. The plan's own non-indications do not describe my case.** CMM-606 states:

> "Non-Indications CMM.SP.NI.606.4 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Lumbar microdiscectomy (laminectomy, hemilaminectomy, and laminoplasty) performed without meeting the criteria in the General Guidelines (Credentialed Spine Surgeon Required);"

and:

> "and, when applicable, Urgent/Emergent Indications/ Conditions) and the criteria in the applicable procedure-specific section (initial microdiscectomy or repeat microdiscectomy) is considered not medically necessary."

The non-indication applies where the criteria are *not* met. My file contains documented conservative care, documented examination findings, and imaging that identifies a specific compressed nerve root. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

I also want to be straightforward with the reviewer: I have quoted the plan only where I have the plan's exact language in front of me. Some of the CMM-606 criteria text I have is partial, and where I have not quoted the plan, I am describing my own medical records in my own words rather than characterizing policy language I cannot verify. If Cigna is relying on a specific criterion in CMM-606 that I have not addressed, I ask that the specific criterion and the reason it was considered unmet be identified in writing so I can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Okafor. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for:

1. A written explanation identifying each CMM-606 criterion found to be unmet and the specific records reviewed;
2. The name and specialty of the clinician who conducted the review;
3. A copy of the clinical criteria applied to my request; and
4. Information about my right to further appeal, including external review.

I understand my appeal must be received by **January 27, 2027** (180 days from the July 31, 2026 notice). I am submitting this appeal through my plan's appeal process at **my.cigna.com**, and I can also be reached by phone regarding this appeal; Cigna's member line is **1-800-244-6224**, or the number on my ID card. If a mailed copy is required, I will use the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. My surgeon's office has advised me it can provide the operative plan, the physical therapy discharge note, the injection record, and the June 8, 2026 MRI report on request.

Thank you for taking a second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Jennings**
